distractors.reason: We don't say 'big review'. 'Big' describes size: a big house, a big problem.
'Strong' is used with coffee, opinions and arguments: strong coffee, strong opinion. We don't say 'strong review'.
'High' is used with ratings and levels: high rating, high score. We don't say 'high review'.

example_sentence: Many guests left a ___ review about the hotel.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes a veces traducen 'gran' de forma literal y dicen 'big review' en vez del correcto 'positive review' (reseña positiva).
explanation: In English, 'positive' describes a review that says good things. Use 'positive' when the opinion is favorable.

related_collocations.example: He wrote a negative review of the restaurant.
I read an honest review before I bought the phone.
Please leave a review after your visit.

memory_tip: POSITIVE = good, favorable (reviews, feedback, results) | BIG = size (big house, big problem)
